services_intro: Six kinds of land work, scoped to your project and your timing.

steps.title: You send the scope.
steps.text: Call, or use the project form. Tell us the basin, the county, the tract list or the deal, and your timing.

steps.title: We agree the approach.
steps.text: We talk through what the work involves and what drives the cost: the number of tracts, the counties and how far back the record runs.

steps.title: We work the record.
steps.text: We run title all the way to the end of the chain, not just to the first clean deed, including the probate and heirship records where problems tend to sit.

steps.title: You get a report you can act on.
steps.text: Each report states what we found, what it means and what the options are, written so you can hand it straight to an attorney, a lender or a deal team.

standards.title: Certified Professional Landmen
standards.description: Both landmen hold the CPL, the highest credential the American Association of Professional Landmen issues for title and leasing work.

standards.title: The same standard on every file
standards.description: A single tract gets the same care as a multi-county program, and an unclear record is reported as unclear, never filled in with a guess.

standards.title: Conflicts disclosed up front
standards.description: We also help mineral owners with their own leases and division orders. The AAPL Code of Ethics requires us to disclose conflicts, so if one comes up on your project you hear about it at the start.

sample_feature.label: Sample Work
sample_feature.headline: Judge the Work Product First
sample_feature.text: A complete fictional file: a runsheet, an ownership report, a lease acquisition report and a supplemental report that resolves an heirship, with notes on how to read each one. It shows the level of detail your files come back with.

faq.question: What kinds of projects do you take on?
faq.answer: Title research and curative work, lease acquisition and negotiation, A&D due diligence, mineral and royalty management, right-of-way and surface use, and solar and renewable land acquisition.

faq.question: Where do you work?
faq.answer: Our completed files run from Pennsylvania to Washington, across the Appalachian, Gulf Coast, Permian and Michigan basins and the Pacific Northwest. We are based in Duncansville, Pennsylvania, and take work in any state.

faq.question: Who will we be working with?
faq.answer: Rickey or Shannon Matherne, the two Certified Professional Landmen who run the firm. One of them runs your project from the first call to the final report, reviews every file, and is the person you talk to.

faq.question: Can you work to a deal timeline?
faq.answer: Yes. Tell us the closing date when you send the package and we scope the review around it. The findings come back as a clear summary your deal team can act on, and if the record turns up something that affects your timeline, you hear about it as soon as we find it.

faq.question: What will it cost?
faq.answer: It depends on what the record holds: the number of tracts, the counties involved and how far back the title has to be run. Heirship questions and missing or unclear records take more time. Send us the scope and we will tell you what the work involves, and we keep you posted if the record turns up something that changes it.

faq.question: What does the finished work look like?
faq.answer: Runsheets, ownership reports, lease acquisition reports and supplemental reports, each stating what the record shows, what it does not, and what it would take to close the gap. The sample file on this site shows a complete set.

faq_cta.text: Have a deal, a leasing program or a tract list to staff? Send us the scope and a CPL will talk it through with you.
